result:
Both worlds are written, but I haven't run a build or a browser, so nothing here has been compiled or looked at in a render.

## What I built
I computed the direction locally from the existing operators: `GalleryStage` maps to **Brasa** (`EmberReel`) and `StudioIndex` to **Herbario** (`PlateStudy`). I touched no JSON, contract, enum or older CSS file.

### Changed paths
- **`src/components/composition/ExperienceComposition.astro`**
  - It now imports the two new stylesheets as `?raw`, resolves the direction, and appends the matching stylesheet only for 03 or 04.
  - For 03/04, the class list becomes `contextual-site experience-site rich-experience depth-experience artistic-site art-<Dir> page-<kind>`. It no longer carries `experience-*`, `tone-*`, `home-*`, `type-*` or `catalogue-*`.
  - Every page except credits goes through the new `ArtisticPages` component.
  - The credits page keeps its shared markup. I added the art credit list and a film paragraph with the new clip's duration and size, both only for 03/04.
  - For 01/02 and the other profiles, every expression falls back to the original string or markup.
- **`src/components/composition/ArtisticPages.astro`** (new): both homes and the nine interior pages. It reuses `ContextualModule`, `PreviewIntent`, `CommunitySections` and `ExperienceFeatures` with unchanged props. All ids, `data-fact-*`, module attributes and editorial copy are preserved.
- **`src/design/artistic-direction.ts`** (new): operator-to-direction mapping and the list of media each world actually uses, which drives the credits.
- **`src/design/artistic-ember.css`** and **`src/design/artistic-plate.css`** (new): one raw stylesheet per world, so neither world's CSS leaks into the other. They contain the `@font-face` rules (WOFF, `font-display:swap`, local `/fonts/b3-artistic/`) and `@view-transition`.
- I added no new scripts. The only script is the existing `ArtisticVideo` module, and the shared client keeps handling the menu filter, selection, journal filter and nav.

## The two structures
**Brasa (03)** is a night kitchen.
- It's black with a single ember colour (`#ff6a2b`), set in Syne 800 uppercase with DM Sans for text.
- At 1025px and wider there is a fixed 84px left rail with a vertical wordmark, vertical Carta and Reservas links, and Explorar. Below that it becomes a normal top bar.
- The home hero is a split: the stacked "LA / MESA" on the left and the fire film (`120734`) on the right. The film is cropped and magnified 1.45× to hide the stove frame, and it fades in from the left edge.
- After that: an overlapping collage (dough, clay, carafe) with caption tabs, a directory in big rows, a full-width cake band under a giant "SOBREMESA", a journal laid out as large title rows each with a photo, one quote per row in reviews, and the contact section as the only ember plane.
- On the carta page, rows alternate photo and copy.
- The story page puts a full-width image first with the text laid across it in two columns.

**Herbario (04)** is botanical plates on paper.
- It's warm paper (`#f3ece0`), plum ink and wine accent, with a celadon plane and a fig-dusk footer. The type is Bodoni Moda (upright only, because no italic file was staged) with DM Sans.
- The header is a centred masthead.
- The home opens with a huge centred "La Mesa". The parsley and wine-splash photos sit behind the letters, blended into the paper with `multiply`.
- Next come five staggered numbered plates with captions, then a centred house note with a two-column directory.
- A celadon interlude holds the single steam clip (`267`, poster `968657`), followed by a wide figs plate, then the journal as a two-column staggered catalogue, centred reviews, and plain-paper contact.
- The carta is a two-column staggered plate grid.
- The reservas form sits on a celadon plane.
- The story page is one centred column.
- The visit page is ruled rows.
- A page-turn wipe view transition runs between pages; Brasa uses the default fade.

## Media
- **03 uses:** `120734` with poster `'120734-poster'`, `1868396`, `10258355`, `1596417`, `8233676`, `1004255` and `1932466`.
- **04 uses:** `1665402`, `1543170`, `4367047`, `8594421`, `1887240`, `10266737`, `968657`, `943245`, `972271` and clip `267`.
- No photo is shared between the two worlds. I did not use `2481346` (flat citrus wallpaper) or the rejected `143799`.
- The old pizza and old hero video are gone from 03/04. Journal and contact still use the existing approved stock.
- Credits list exactly the ids above with `data-art-credit`, each linked to its Pixabay source page.

## Page coverage (both worlds)
Home, carta, selección, reservas, historia, visita, preguntas, diario, opiniones, contacto and créditos all render. Each has its own head. The images vary by page: visita and opiniones (both worlds), preguntas and selección (Herbario), reservas and historia (both).

## Risks and untested items
- **Build.** I haven't compiled it. Possible build errors are the `slot="scene"` on `ArtisticImage`, the `?raw` CSS imports, and the types in `ArtisticPages`.
- **Dropped classes.** Removing the old operator and tone classes from 03/04 will break any audit or test that selects on them. That is intentional, but Codex should expect it.
- **Fire crop.** The 1.45× magnification and poster crop are guesses from the storyboard. I haven't seen the actual frames. Softness and any leftover white frame edge need a visual check.
- **Steam clip.** I haven't seen clip `267` and chose its poster blind. At 640×360 it will look soft when enlarged. The poster loads eagerly because `ArtisticImage` requires `hero` for it, and the steam film sits mid-page, so it may cost some performance.
- **Multiply cutouts.** Halos around the parsley and wine splash are possible if the white backgrounds aren't clean. I added a soft radial mask as protection.
- **Rail sizing.** Rail text sizes and heights are estimates and need checking at short viewport heights.
- **Syne widths.** The "SOBREMESA" word and the big uppercase h1s use Syne width guesses. They are set to wrap with `overflow-wrap:anywhere`, but overflow is possible at 360px.
- **Journal overrides.** The journal, reviews and collection pages override very specific refinement rules by source order and matching specificity. If a filtered state looks wrong, that's where to look.
- **Contrast.** None of my contrast ratios are measured. They are hand estimates only. The ember plane's small text and the muted-on-celadon text are the ones to check.
- **Mobile and tablet.** I wrote the breakpoints but haven't seen them.
- **View transitions.** The transitions are CSS-only and Chromium-only; they should do nothing elsewhere.
- **Reduced motion.** I turned off the reveal, transitions and hover scale under reduced motion, but haven't tested it.
